foundation: Original baseline geometry; selective reviewed helper extraction only. No candidate tissue simplification inherited.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Distinct portal and arterial inputs share sinusoidal circulation and drain centrally.

steps.text: Identify both input vessel walls and their entries.
Follow sinusoidal channels from inflow through the lobular parenchyma to central outflow.
Restore hepatocyte plates to identify the tissue bordering the blood path.

schematic_limitations: No tracer particles, CFD, pulsation, perfusion time or quantitative mixing fraction is modeled.
A lumen that appears to touch another is not validated as patent. Downstream hepatic veins are described, outside the block.
Do not present one portal profile per corner as a universal human section.

functional_sequences.mechanism: The hepatocyte has distinct blood-facing and canalicular interfaces; secreted bile drains through Hering to the portal duct.

steps.text: Identify the blood-facing hepatocyte surface and the canalicular space at the adjacent-cell interface.
Trace canalicular drainage through the lining transition at Hering into the portal ductule.
Compare peripheral-to-central blood drainage with bile drainage toward the portal duct.

schematic_limitations: Bile is secreted by hepatocytes throughout the tissue; it does not enter the lobule through the central vein.
Counterflow is the aggregate relationship of separate networks; no paired one-to-one antiparallel pipes implied.
Existing Hering mixed-lining explanation is retained as baseline intent; source-derived geometry must show the transition, not a naked connector.
No transporter kinetics, active canalicular contraction or obstruction simulation is implemented.

functional_sequences.mechanism: The perisinusoidal interval permits exchange between plasma and hepatocyte surfaces while the canalicular interface remains separate.

steps.text: Find lumen and the endothelial boundary; distinguish the interval external to it from the blood lumen.
Identify hepatocyte processes on the blood-facing surface and compare the separate canalicular interface.
Locate Kupffer cell on the luminal side and stellate cell in the perisinusoidal compartment; describe macrophage versus support/storage identity.

schematic_limitations: The exchange detail requires reviewed selective inset extraction or equivalent model-specific construction; baseline patches alone do not teach the complete relationship.
Fine pores, microvilli and Disse interval must be marked as enlarged ultrastructural teaching features, not ordinary H&E-scale observations.
Empty Disse space is an interstitial compartment, not a second blood tube or bile lumen.
Normal view must not imply capillarization, fibrotic collagen accumulation or activated myofibroblasts.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Filtered sinusoidal fluid joins interstitial drainage toward portal lymphatics.

steps.text: Locate the interstitial side of the endothelial lining.
Connect Disse conceptually to periportal interstitium and the lymphatic vessel in the portal tract.
Distinguish the interstitial path from an endothelial-lined lymphatic; retain the limiting relationship without making a sealed fence.

schematic_limitations: The model displays the major portal route; sublobular and capsular drainage remain outside its scope.
No dedicated baseline Disse/Mall selectable mesh exists; do not invent an app selection key or a long fabricated lymph tube alongside every sinusoid.
No fluid-production rate, pressure, ascites or immune-trafficking kinetics is represented.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Inflow-to-outflow exposure order organizes spatially varying hepatocyte programs.

steps.text: Establish inflow and central outflow landmarks.
Reveal the acinus diagram and identify upstream zone 1, intermediate zone 2 and downstream zone 3.
Explain qualitatively declining oxygen exposure together with contextual signaling and zonated gene expression; distinguish observed human patterns from mechanistic animal studies.

schematic_limitations: Neither colored hepatocyte domains nor overlay boundaries are physiological walls or measured oxygen fields.
Do not teach universal first-injury rules or a diagnostic disease simulation.
Do not assert exclusive zone-specific gluconeogenesis, lipid metabolism or toxin metabolism from historical labels; current human evidence requires context.
Classical lobule, acinus and bile-centered portal organization are conceptual units, not three physical capsules.

required_text_corrections.zone_1: First exposed near portal inflow, with comparatively higher oxygen exposure. Functional programs vary with human context and species; this schematic does not assign exclusive metabolic tasks or a universal injury order.
required_text_corrections.zone_2: Intermediate position along the inflow-to-outflow path. It is an explanatory region, not a sharp biological compartment or a unique disease diagnosis.
required_text_corrections.zone_3: Downstream toward central outflow, with comparatively lower oxygen exposure and zonated metabolic/signaling programs. Relative susceptibility is context-dependent; no universal first-injury sequence is modeled.
required_text_corrections.lymph: Portal lymphatics drain interstitial fluid originating in sinusoidal exchange. Portal drainage is the represented major route; sublobular and capsular routes are omitted.
required_text_corrections.scale: Lobular organization is schematic; cells, canaliculi, pores and Disse interface are enlarged by different amounts. Do not use this mixed-scale teaching geometry to measure human microscopic dimensions.
